description.narrative: VAHSI facilitates early access to safe and effective COVID-19 vaccines to save lives, reduce illness and is intended to make a critical contribution to recovery within the Indo-Pacific. The activities funded by the Initiative address requests for assistance from partner Governments, supported by Australian technical expertise, and are designed in consultation with Posts and in-country partners. In 2020 and 2021, the focus of the initiative was procuring and delivering COVID-19 vaccines to countries. In 2022, as the needs of partner Governments shifted, VAHSI’s scope was expanded to include routine and remedial immunisation for other vaccine-preventable diseases.

description.narrative: Australia’s Vaccine Access and Health Security Initiative (VAHSI) worked with partners across the Indo-Pacific region to improve disease prevention and control through better COVID-19 and routine immunisation programs. Australian support ensured immunisation programs were delivered in a safe and timely manner, with a focus on making sure that doses reached everyone – including women, children, the elderly, people with a disability and remote or hard to access communities. ‍ Examples included UNICEF supporting routine immunisation of over 2,600 children in Vanuatu, and making sure 500 people in Tuvalu access to information about safe and effective vaccination. In Vietnam, UNICEF taught 143 community champions to advocate for immunisation, who then trained a further 215 local champions to support immunisation in their communities. UNICEF support in Timor-Leste helped the government achieve over 90% first-dose COVID-19 vaccine coverage.

In 2022, Australia supported 12 partner countries (6 in Pacific, 6 in Southeast Asia) to improve responses to health security threats by increasing community understanding of the importance and safety of COVID-19 vaccination. This reached over 13 million people, including at-risk groups. Australia also worked with UNICEF to assist partner governments in Fiji, Kiribati, Solomon Islands and Tuvalu increase demand in for COVID-19 vaccinations in target populations through public information campaigns.

In 2022-23, Australia supported immunisation of people by delivering over 12 million COVID-19 vaccine doses to countries in the Pacific and Southeast Asia. This included delivering paediatric doses to help ensure children had access to safe and effective COVID-19 vaccination – in the Philippines Australia delivered 6 million paediatric doses ahead of schools reopening in the second half of 2022, and in Vietnam we delivered over 3 million paediatric doses. We also delivered over 450,000 adult COVID-19 vaccine doses to Thailand, over 224,100 adult and paediatric doses to Fiji, and 2,200 adult and paediatric doses to Tonga.
